title: Statistical Slice Lifecycle and Comms Playbook (working)
summary: Working notes for a cross-functional lifecycle to define, instrument, and communicate statistical slices (cohorts) for canaries and A/B tests. Focused on power planning, early-warning signals, and lightweight comms templates for rapid rollback/mitigation.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight operational pattern for treating 'slices' (user cohorts, traffic partitions, input-type buckets) as first-class experiment units. It focuses on three commonly muddled areas: 1) statistical power planning for small/rare slices, 2) signal instrumentation and escalation thresholds, and 3) comms/decision templates so product, SRE, and CS act in lockstep during rollouts.

Audience:
- Product owners running feature/platform rollouts
- Eng SRE owners who configure routing & SLAs
- Observability/telemetry engineers who own metric definitions
- CS & support who triage customer reports

Quick decision rules (working):
- If a slice has < 0.5% of total traffic, treat it as low-power: require paired synthetic traffic or extended observation window (>= 48h) before major changes.
- For safety-critical slices (privacy-regulated regions, paid-tier customers), require a canary + shadow run even if slice is small.
- Use two-tier alarms: (A) immediate SLO breach (P95 latency, error-rate spike > 2x baseline), (B) quality drift (policy-based flags, e.g., toxicity or hallucination increase > 50% on evaluation prompts).

Definitions (for shared vocabulary):
- Slice: a selector over requests (route, country, feature-flag, prompt-template, device).
- Exposure: cumulative fraction of traffic that has been subject to the variant under test.
- Power window: time or sample size used to compute statistical confidence for a slice.

Instrumenting slices (practical checklist):
- telemetry: instrument slice_id on every request and response (string tag) and increment per-token counters for generation workloads.
- metrics: define per-slice baseline metrics: request_count, p50/p95 latency, error_rate, tokens_per_request, rerank_rate, eval_quality_score.
- evaluation: have a small, curated prompt set per slice (10–30 prompts) that runs on each rollout stage and reports quality regressions.
- synthetic traffic: maintain a lightweight harness that can pump 1–2% additional traffic into a slice for power testing without affecting real users.

Statistical power cheatsheet (practical heuristics):
- Minimum sample size per variant per slice: 1k requests for broad quality signals; 5k for subtle quality deltas (3–5% lift/delta).
- If you cannot reach minimum sample in N hours, either increase exposure (temporary ramp) or move to longer observation (narrow confidence).
- For rare-event metrics (safety flags), prefer Poisson/negative-binomial modeling; expect wide CIs and rely on evaluation prompts for decisioning.

Example flow: small premium cohort (0.8% traffic)
1) Stage 0 (shadow): run variant in shadow for 12h, run eval prompt set every hour.
2) Stage 1 (canary 1% of cohort): route 1% of cohort, synthetic boost enabled to reach 1k samples in 6h. Monitor immediate SLOs + eval quality.
3) Stage 2 (ramp): if no alerts and eval delta < 1.5% negative, ramp to 10% of cohort across 24–48h.
4) Full roll: subject to business owner sign-off, rollback window, and monitoring retention criteria.

Escalation thresholds (examples to put in alerting):
- Latency P95 > baseline P95 * 1.5 for 5 consecutive minutes for the slice.
- Error rate (5xx or internal error) > baseline + 0.5 percentage points for slice for 10 minutes.
- Eval_quality_score delta <= -2% absolute vs baseline on the curated prompt set in two consecutive runs.
- Manual signal: "floor reports" > 3 support tickets referencing feature within 2h.

Runbook snippets (what to say & who to call):
- Initial triage (first 15m): on pager, SRE looks at routing & infra; product checks experiment cohort and feature-flag config; obs engineer validates metric tags.
- Decision within 30m: if immediate SLO breach or obvious data corruption -> rollback to previous stable model/version.
- Decision within 2h: if noisy or ambiguous quality drift -> pause ramp, enable synthetic traffic to reproduce, open a dedicated Slack huddle with product, SRE, and model owners.

Comms templates (canary incident) - SHORT: 
- Subject: Canary Alert: [feature] [slice] — latency/error/quality spike
- Body: TL;DR variant X rolled to Y% of slice Z. We see P95 latency up 80% and error_rate +1.2pp. Action: pausing ramp and routing variant to shadow. Oncall: @sre-oncall. Owner: Maya (product). Next update: 30m.

Decision matrix (quick reference):
- Immediate rollback: SLO breach (tier A) OR data corruption (bad payloads/garbage outputs).
- Pause & investigate: eval-quality delta moderate and support signal present, but infra healthy.
- Continue ramp: no SLO breach, eval within noise, and no user-impacting tickets.

Gating ceremony checklist (pre-rollout, 15–30m sync):
- Confirm slice selectors and telemetry tags are correct. (obs engineer)
- Confirm synthetic harness available and tested. (qa/solutions eng)
- Confirm eval prompt set loaded & baseline computed. (applied-ml)
- Confirm rollback playbook & traffic-steering runbook accessible. (sre)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we standardize an eval_quality_score across model families? (applied-ml to propose a normalized schema)
- Should we automate synthetic traffic boost via the console? (product + platform follow-up)
- Decide standard min exposure thresholds per SKU and per region (billing & revenue teams?)

Example quick SQLs (obs team) - these are intentionally rough and local to our metrics schema:
- counts per slice per variant (last 24h):
  SELECT slice, variant, count(*) as requests
  FROM requests_v2
  WHERE ts > now() - interval '24 hours'
  GROUP BY slice, variant;
- eval delta per slice:
  SELECT slice, avg(eval_score) FILTER (WHERE variant='control') as baseline, avg(eval_score) FILTER (WHERE variant='treatment') as treatment
  FROM eval_results
  WHERE ts > now() - interval '48 hours'
  GROUP BY slice;

Notes on minimizing false positives in alerts:
- Require alert conditions to be met across two independent signals (metric + eval prompt set OR metric + support volume) before auto-triggering high-severity pager.
- Suppress high-sensitivity alerts during known load tests or external incidents.

Hand-off checklist after rollback (post-incident):
- Write brief postmortem (owner: product) within 48 hours.
- Capture lessons in the slice's Confluence page and link to the experiment row in our experiments table.
- Schedule a 1-hour postmortem readout with SRE, product, and CS within 5 working days if customer-impacting.

Appendix: quick templates for experiment entries (for the experiment tracking sheet)
- Experiment name: [feature] — [slice] — [date]
- Hypothesis: short statement + expected metric delta
- Min sample per variant (computed): [number]
- Synthetic traffic enabled: yes/no
- Eval prompt set id: [confluence/eval-id]
- Monitoring owners & slack channel: #prod-flighting, @sre-oncall

This is intentionally a concise, operational-first working doc. Follow-ups: convert to a checklist/templatized page in Confluence and wire alerting templates into the console's rollout UI.

Notes-to-self: preserve the distinction between 'slice power' and 'business criticality' — a tiny premium paid cohort may be low-power statistically but high-priority from an SLA & revenue perspective; treat accordingly.

-- end --
